evidence: Cic. Top. 22: pariēs vel solidus vel fornicātus (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Div. 1.48: a solid gold column, against a gilded one (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Solid through and through, against hollow, gilded or liquid: aurō solidī, of solid gold (Verg. A. 2.765); in solidum coīre, to set solid. It also means whole and entire (see whole).

evidence: Lewis & Short, s.v. firmus: firm in opposition to frail
terms.comment: Solid as strong and stable: a table, a wall, a friendship.

phrases.latin: nam etiam maximum solida nōn recēpērunt, rūrsus ārida et corripī facilia scintillam quoque fovent ūsque in incendium
phrases.english: for solid logs won’t take even a great flame, while dry stuff that catches easily nurses even a spark into a blaze

phrases.latin: perque coāgula dēnsa liquor in solidum coit
phrases.english: and with thick rennet the liquid sets solid

sources: Lewis & Short: solidus · Lewis & Short: firmus
Quotations from the Latinitas loci collections (loci-seneca-epistulae, loci-prudentius), checked against the editions named there.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, with its references, in the house spelling (macrons, consonantal j); they have not been checked against a modern edition.
